title: Portal frame, axial deformation neglected: vertical and horizontal load

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. a (0, 0), b (0, 5), c (8, 5), d (8, 0) m; a and d fixed. Columns I = 50e6 mm^4, beam I = 200e6 mm^4, E = 200,000 MPa. The source neglects axial deformation. The engine always includes axial deformation; the source's assumption is represented by a member area of 1e8 mm^2 for every member (four orders of magnitude above the areas the source uses for the same members elsewhere, 4e3 and 6e3 mm^2), one value for all problems of this kind. The remaining axial flexibility changes the targets by less than 1e-5 of their value (measured by repeating the analysis with 1e9 mm^2; see README.md), far below their printed precision. Combination W: 2 kN/m downward on the beam; combination H: 2.5 kN (+x) at b and at c. First order, no shear deformation. Section properties the source does not give because they do not enter its plane model (Iy, J; A where stated) are placeholders that do not influence the targets.
